**Google Interview Presentation Prompt** 

We’re excited you’ve reached the Presentation stage of the **Practice Customer Engineering** interview process. The content below provides background information, instructions, assessment details and best practices for your presentation. For questions regarding your interview schedule, please contact your Recruiter. 

Background 

The **Practice Customer Engineer** serves as a domain expert responsible for accelerating technical wins and adoption of complex, specialized workloads. You will leverage your deep expertise in our most strategic product areas to be hands-on developing prototypes, proofs-of-concept, and demos to sell new, highly specialized solutions to customers. You will solve practice-specific customer challenges and provide a critical feedback loop to influence customers and product development. 

In this 45-minute, 1:1 interview, you’ll be assessed on your domain-specific technical acumen, consultative skills, and your ability to deliver a targeted presentation of your choosing. You will spend **30 minutes presenting** and **10-15 minutes of Q\&A** regarding your presentation content. 

Assessment 

The purpose of this part of the interview process is to assess your ability in the following areas: 

● Domain-specific technical acumen 

● Hands-on keyboard skills 

● Identifying customer solutions 

● Engaging with your audience 

● Conveying measurable business value 

● Effectively handling questions 

**Scenario 1: Financial Services \- Agent Development (ADK)** 

**Problem Statement**   
A fintech company provides personal loans ranging from $5,000 to $100,000. They currently process 10,000 loan applications daily, with an average approval time of 48 hours. This delay is causing customer churn—competitors are offering same-day approvals. 

**Current workflow:** 

1\. Customer submits application via web/mobile (basic info: income, employer, loan amount) 2\. Operations team manually queries credit bureaus (Equifax, TransUnion, Experian) 

3\. Employment verification team calls employers or uses third-party verification APIs 4\. Underwriters cross-reference internal policy documents to determine eligibility 

5\. Senior underwriter reviews borderline cases 

6\. Decision communicated to customer 

**The bottleneck:** 

● Policy documents change weekly (new regulations, risk appetite adjustments) 

● Underwriters spend 30 minutes per application navigating 200+ pages of policy PDFs ● The internal policy engine is a legacy rule system that can't keep pace with policy changes ● 70% of applications are 'straightforward' (clear approve/deny based on policies) but still take 48 hours 

**External APIs available:** 

● Credit Bureau API: Returns credit score, payment history, outstanding debts, inquiries (latency: 2-3 seconds) 

● Employment Verification API: Confirms current employment, salary range, tenure (latency: 5-30 seconds, may require async callback) 

● Fraud Detection API: Real-time fraud signals, identity verification (latency: 1 second) ● Bank Statement Analysis API: Parses uploaded statements for income verification (latency: 10-15 seconds) 

**Internal resources:** 

● Policy documents in Confluence (200+ pages, updated weekly) 

● Historical decisions database (5 years of approve/deny decisions with outcomes) 

● Risk scoring model (custom ML model returning a score 0-100) 

**The customer wants:** An agentic system using Google's Agent Development Kit that can: 

1\. Orchestrate calls to multiple external APIs in parallel where possible 

2\. Apply current business rules from policy documents (these change frequently) 

3\. Generate a structured risk report with clear reasoning chain 

4\. Auto-approve/deny 70% of 'straightforward' applications in under 5 minutes 

5\. Route complex cases to human underwriters with pre-populated analysis 

**Key requirements:** 

● Must maintain complete audit trail for regulatory compliance 

● Each application must be isolated—no data leakage between sessions 

● System must handle API failures gracefully (credit bureau downtime is common) 

● Reasoning must be explainable—regulators may ask why a decision was made 

● Must respect rate limits on external APIs (credit bureau: 100 calls/minute) 

**Constraints:** 

● Cannot store credit data beyond the session—must be stateless for PII compliance ● Must support PCI-DSS compliance for any financial data handling 

● Human escalation path must be seamless (no re-entry of data) 

![][image2]careers.google.com  
**Design an agent architecture using ADK. Sketch out the sub-agents, their responsibilities, tool definitions, and how you would handle state management and error recovery.** 

Your Audience 

You, the domain specialist, have been engaged to build that architecture and present it to the customer’s domain expert. You are presenting the validated proof-of-concept and final technical design to the **customer’s domain expert (Technical Stakeholder)** and their **VP of Strategy (Business Stakeholder)**. Your interviewer will ask questions to represent both perspectives. 

Your Presentation 

We recommend your presentation to follow the layout and flow below. You are welcome to create a slide presentation, screen share, or use another format to showcase your solution. Your presentation is intended to be covered in **30 minutes** with **10-15 minutes of Q\&A regarding your presentation content**. The mock customer meeting should not exceed **45 minutes**, including interactions and questions from the “customer”. 

● **Title & context:** Introductions and setting the stage for the specific practice scenario. ● **The specialized challenge**: Clearly define the "unblocker." Why was an off-the-shelf solution impossible? 

● **Technical deep-dive / live demonstration:** Show the custom code, scripts, or novel architecture used to resolve the challenge. Demonstrate your "hands-on" proficiency. 

● **Architectural decisions & trade-offs:** Defend your design to the technical expert. Why this custom approach over others? 

● **Business & strategic value:** Translate the technical win into ROI or competitive advantage for the VP of Strategy. 

● **Implementation & next steps:** High-level roadmap for moving the prototype to production ramp. 

Presentation Logistics 

● **Important:** Be sure **not** to include confidential information in your presentation; including the name of the customer example being used. Avoid using logos, screenshots or imagery that could breach confidentiality. Please make the best decision based on your current workplace agreements. 

● While our goal is to evaluate your ability to step into a Google Cloud CE role, this interview is not meant to be an exhaustive demonstration of your mastery of Google's product features or naming conventions. 

![][image3]careers.google.com  
Please feel free to leverage your experience with other public cloud providers and products in the market as part of your presentation. 

● You’re welcome to use any presentation software (including but not limited to: Google Slides, PPT, Adobe, Prezi, Keynote). Please note that certain software may take over your entire presentation window. Be sure to practice presenting via Google Meet before your interview. 

● Practice your presentation without your notes. You may use notes during your presentation, but know that if you share your screen, the interviewers may be able to see them. 

Best Practices 

● Build your presentation with simplicity and intention. The panel will assess verbal communication and presentation content and structure. 

● We want this to be fun, not burdensome\! The presentation should take no more than approximately four hours to prepare. 

● Anticipate and prepare for questions you might be asked during and after you finish. ● Practice\! Your delivery should be conversational but professional. Let your Recruiter know if you have any questions about your presentation format.
